main_issue: How to handle D's strong-smelling cooking (sambal belacan): A wants it restricted, B and C want a fan out the window, D wants to keep cooking.

A-B.evidence: A (11) doubts the fan, B (12) says try it. A's time restriction (15) is accepted by D, and B (18) says it is only partial. B (20) returns to the fan, which A never endorsed.

A-C.evidence: C backs the fan (9, 13, 21) while A says a fan won't be enough (11). Neither disputes the other's concern, and A's timing deal (15-17) is not endorsed by C (19).

A-D.evidence: A and D agree the fan won't be enough (10-11). D agrees to cook after 7 on weekdays or on weekends (16), and A thanks D (17). A softens to 'not saying never cook' (15).

B-C.evidence: B drops the yard-facing fan after C's objection (8), and C says it might work (9). They then jointly push the fan (12-13, 20-21).

B-D.evidence: D doubts the fan and asks why she must set one up each time (10, 14). B keeps pushing it (12, 20). D accepts timing, which B says doesn't solve his problem (18).

C-D.evidence: C's laundry concern (3) and support for the fan (13, 21) face D's doubt (10, 14). D's timing deal (16) is not enough for C (19).
